# Curated Paper Theatre model sources

This is a compact selection of 39 unmodified original creator models:

- 24 Quaternius Medieval Village MegaKit Standard environment FBXs.
- 11 ordinary harbour/household Quaternius Fantasy Props MegaKit Standard FBXs.
- 3 ordinary Kenney Furniture Kit GLBs: one bed, table and open bookcase.
- 1 ordinary Quaternius Medieval Village Pack brass bell FBX.

Every retained pack is CC0 1.0 Universal. The three larger packs retain their
exact original creator license notices. The bell retains the complete canonical
CC0 legal code and the explicit primary creator webpage/release grants; its
separate Drive notice returned quota-exceeded HTML. Each pack's README and
SOURCE.json records this evidence, original source/download URL, archive and
per-file hashes, role, fit assessment and small required adjustments. The
selection includes the models and their required material images. To obtain a
complete source archive, follow the creator link in that pack's SOURCE.json.

The selection follows the Paper Theatre references: shallow modular facades,
wood decks/rails, stone trim/stairs, a pitched tile roof and simple everyday
props. Use the planned cream, ink/navy, brass and muted-brick paper materials,
then check scene scale and pivots. Creator normal-map alternatives are retained
where relevant. No newer .blend sources, fantasy towers, weapons, vehicles,
electronics or generated substitute meshes are included.

All 39 files imported successfully into a separate Blender 5.2.2 LTS background
factory-startup process: 41 mesh objects and zero unresolved referenced images
after original-source relinking. Sixteen stock-material previews and one Bell
opacity-only preview were rendered and visually inspected. Bell's imported
Alpha=0 was restored to 1 only in the temporary scene to expose its silhouette;
its original brass colour and geometry were retained. Source bytes and all 77
source-file hashes remain unchanged. UE 4.27.2 validation is pending.

Kenney furniture imports at a smaller scale; match it to Elias. FBX origins are
(0,0,0) while bounds can be offset, and the bed has three child meshes. Book and
bottle colour attributes are present but unconnected in the imported material
graphs. The bell needs opaque material alpha and has no UV layers; use a simple
or world-coordinate paper surface, or small UV work in a derived copy. The bell
also needs a suitable suspension pivot and mounting bracket/rope. Timber bracing,
a steep roof, a deep window frame and a round stool seat are source-shape caveats
to review during placement and the paper-material pass.

Important remaining roles are elderly Elias in an ordinary brown overcoat, the
defining tapered street lantern, a complete hoist/crank/pulley, an open ledger,
a suitable potted plant, damaged/torn paper pieces and background sailboats.

Use each pack's `SOURCE.json` for asset provenance and verified import details.
Project attribution is recorded in
[ASSET-CREDITS.csv](../../../Docs/ASSET-CREDITS.csv).
